title: 2026 Ceva Edge Symposium: Building Intelligence Beyond the Cloud - Semiwiki
gist: Ceva's 2026 Edge Symposium (Hsinchu Nov 2, Shanghai Nov 5) will pitch its 'Connect, Sense, Infer' IP framework as the building blocks for Physical AI and Agentic AI, backed by Ceva's claimed footprint of 22 billion shipped devices and 400+ customers, while the piece flags unresolved security and accountability questions as autonomy moves to the edge.

insights.claim: Ceva structures its intelligent-edge-system pitch around a three-part 'Connect, Sense, Infer' model: Connect covers wireless technologies (Bluetooth, Wi-Fi, ultra-wideband, cellular IoT, 5G, satellite); Sense covers computer vision, audio, radar, motion detection, and sensor fusion; Infer covers the on-device AI processing that turns signals into decisions.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: A reusable mental model for evaluating any edge-AI IP vendor's product breadth — Ceva is positioning across all three layers rather than owning just one, a structurally broader addressable footprint than single-layer competitors.
insights.quote: “Connect” covers wireless technologies such as Bluetooth, Wi-Fi, ultra-wideband, cellular IoT, 5G, and satellite communications.
insights.locator: At the symposium, Ceva will present its “Connect, Sense, Infer” model

insights.claim: Bringing connectivity, sensing, and inference together lets an edge device not just collect information but understand its environment and take appropriate action, which the article frames as the functional definition of moving from a passive sensor to an autonomous agent.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Defines the bar for what counts as a genuine 'agentic' edge product versus a simple connected sensor — useful for filtering marketing claims from real capability across the sector.
insights.locator: Bringing these capabilities together allows a device not only to collect information

themes.theme: Structural Shift: Cloud AI to Physical and Agentic AI

insights.claim: The article's thesis is that generative AI first gained broad attention through cloud-based services, but many future AI systems will need to perceive and act directly in the physical world, requiring on-device rather than cloud-only processing.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Frames edge AI silicon/IP as the next infrastructure layer investors should track after the cloud AI compute buildout, since it targets a distinct and growing set of physical-world use cases.
insights.quote: Generative AI first gained broad attention through cloud-based services, but many future systems will need to perceive and act in the physical world.
insights.locator: The symposium matters because AI is entering a new stage

insights.claim: The piece distinguishes 'Physical AI' (connecting computation to machines, vehicles, appliances, and wearables) from 'Agentic AI' (systems that pursue objectives, make decisions, and coordinate actions with less continuous human direction), positioning both as requiring timely, trustworthy edge data.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Gives investors a clean taxonomy to classify edge-AI product announcements (Physical AI = embodiment, Agentic AI = autonomy) rather than treating 'edge AI' as one undifferentiated category.
insights.locator: Physical AI connects computation to machines, vehicles, appliances

insights.claim: Processing data locally at the edge reduces latency, conserves network bandwidth, improves reliability, protects sensitive data, and lowers power consumption versus continuously streaming raw sensor data to the cloud.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: A concise five-benefit checklist for why specific workloads (safety-critical, privacy-sensitive, bandwidth-constrained) migrate off cloud inference to local silicon.
insights.locator: This approach can reduce latency, conserve network bandwidth

insights.claim: Ceva reports its technologies have shipped in more than 22 billion devices and are used by over 400 customers, evidence the author cites as giving the symposium relevance beyond a single product announcement.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: A hard scale metric (22bn units, 400+ customers) that quantifies Ceva's existing IP licensing footprint, useful as a baseline to track growth or share shifts in the edge-AI IP licensing market.
insights.quote: Ceva reports that its technologies have shipped in more than 22 billion devices and are used by over 400 customers
insights.locator: Ceva reports that its technologies have shipped

insights.claim: The 2026 Ceva Edge Symposium is scheduled for November 2 in Hsinchu, Taiwan and November 5 in Shanghai, China, deliberately targeting the two major Asian semiconductor and electronics manufacturing ecosystems.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Venue choice signals Ceva's core customer base sits within Taiwan/China's device and chip manufacturing supply chains rather than in Western OEMs.
insights.locator: Scheduled for November 2 in Hsinchu, Taiwan, and November 5 in Shanghai, China

themes.theme: Adoption Reality Check and Open Risks

insights.claim: The success of edge AI depends on more than an impressive algorithm: developers must combine processors, sensors, wireless systems, software, development tools, and power-management techniques within strict cost and energy limits, which is why live demonstrations matter for judging real commercial maturity.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: A due-diligence checklist for evaluating edge-AI vendor claims: demand end-to-end system demos, not isolated algorithm benchmarks, before crediting commercial readiness.
insights.quote: the success of edge AI depends on more than an impressive algorithm.
insights.locator: Live demonstrations from Ceva and its ecosystem partners

insights.claim: Greater device autonomy from Physical AI and Agentic AI introduces unresolved questions about security, accuracy, accountability, and human oversight that the article says the industry still needs to address alongside technical performance.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: A caution flag inside an otherwise promotional preview: regulatory and safety scrutiny of autonomous edge/agentic systems is a real overhang, not a solved problem, even as the hardware ships.
insights.quote: greater autonomy introduces difficult questions about security, accuracy, accountability, and human oversight.
insights.locator: However, greater autonomy introduces difficult questions
